title: Moyogi: A Memory-Centric Accelerator for Low-Latency Random Forest Inference on Embedded Devices
problem: Random Forest inference on resource-constrained embedded devices must maintain low latency as model size grows; state-of-the-art memory-centric approaches suffer from latency degradation with increasing RF complexity.
motivation: Edge computing for IoT and critical applications like autonomous vehicles and smart healthcare requires real-time, low-latency ML inference without cloud transmission overhead.
method: Designs the hardware accelerator and software together to run Random Forest inference (making predictions using decision-tree ensembles) efficiently on embedded devices by organizing computation around memory access patterns. Tests different configurations: varying the depth of individual decision trees and trying different hardware designs, using a resource estimation model to predict how much computing hardware each option needs. Systematically explores these combinations to find which one delivers the fastest prediction time for a given Random Forest model.
key_novelty: Co-optimizing decision tree structure and hardware architecture using resource estimates to achieve low-latency Random Forest inference on embedded devices.
contributions: Moyogi framework for hardware-software codesigned memory-centric RF accelerators
Resource estimation model enabling Design Space Exploration of RF configurations
Exploration of variable-depth decision tree optimization for RF inference
3.88x geomean latency reduction on IoT datasets vs state-of-the-art approaches
primary_theme: Memory-centric Random Forest acceleration for edge inference
